# Editability Audit
Date: 2026-11-13
Repository: therealvacations/therealvacations
Branch: main
Commit: affdde288e3fae6e6bdf3ea12115819e8d3f8736

## Summary
- Total pages audited: 54 standalone HTML pages, plus 2 shared fragments (56 HTML files); 52 public/member/supplier/host/auth pages scored; 2 admin-only pages reviewed but exempt.
- Pages fully editable from admin: 0
- Pages with gaps: 52 (all scored pages)
- Total hardcoded values found: 8,087 enumerated literal/declaration occurrences (includes immutable fallback copies behind existing bindings)
- Total values correctly sourced from Supabase: 55 distinct confirmed source-level table/column bindings in the shared content loaders (conservative minimum, listed below; not a live-data count)
- Editability score: 0% (fully editable scored pages / all scored pages; not a ratio of incomparable literal and database-field counts)
- Overall: FAIL

### Method, counting rules, and limits

This is a static source audit of the named commit, not an authenticated Supabase Table Editor/Supamode or production-browser test. Every file under `public/` was inventoried; all HTML, embedded JS/CSS, all root `js/*.js`, root build helpers, all six `api/` JavaScript files, `vercel.json`, and every migration were inspected with source extraction and targeted manual tracing. No application code, migrations, prices, payment logic, or configuration was changed. Binary assets are inventoried at the end; pixels are not editable text or theme tokens.

The hardcoded inventory is a reproducible **lower-bound occurrence inventory**, not a claim that semantic free-form source has an objectively exact total. Each row is one text fragment, content-bearing attribute, JS content string, or theme declaration at a file/line. Identical value/category occurrences on the same line are deduplicated (minified files can contain multiple such occurrences). Currency literals and strings containing monetary amounts are omitted per request; their surrounding labels/destinations/deadlines remain in scope. Selectors, enum/status codes, allowlists, protocol strings, auth redirects, DOM IDs, layout mechanics such as `display`, and API routing constants are not editable-content findings. Theme declarations include requested palette/spacing/typography/shadow/radius tokens, not every CSS property. Human-readable templates can be split around interpolations. The JS inventory includes server-returned user messages (admin API responses, health diagnostics, provider strings and technical constants are excluded); administrator-only UI copy and editor default values are excluded. A bound HTML fallback is explicitly marked and **is not alleged to be uneditable in the healthy populated-data path**; its fallback value remains code-only and cannot be revised through the dashboard.

“Correctly sourced” is a conservative inventory of distinct content-bearing table/column bindings in the shared loaders, not every record, package price, operational ID, or nested JSON leaf. Source-wired is not proof of a deployed module, existing live column, valid RLS, or a working admin save. The 0% page score avoids presenting an inflated token-level percentage. No access to the live Supabase schema, data, permissions, Supamode configuration, Edge Function deployments, or Stripe state was available; these are explicitly unverified, not assumed absent. Migration absence is **not** evidence that a live table was deleted.

`site_content[key=page.NAME].value.PATH` below is a **proposed target**, not a discovered implementation. `global_theme` is likewise proposed/unimplemented in this tree. Existing `site_settings` JSON fields and actual data tables should be reused rather than duplicated.

### Decisive repository-wide blockers

1. **Shared modules are outside the published tree.** `vercel.json:2–3` sets an empty build command and `outputDirectory: public`; there is no tracked `public/js/`. `/js/site-settings.js`, `/js/content-public.js`, `/js/supabase-client.js`, `/js/auth.js`, and all admin modules exist only at repository-root `js/`. Both root build helpers contain copy/injection steps, but neither is invoked by `package.json` or this Vercel configuration. Source-level content bindings therefore cannot be assumed available under the checked-in deployment configuration. This is a static configuration finding, not an observed production HTTP response; a dashboard override or externally generated artifact could differ.
2. **No `site_content` implementation or `global_theme` reader.** There is no matching table declaration in migrations and no `.from('site_content')` or `global_theme` consumer in public/shared JS. Creating keys in a dashboard alone will not change any page. All scored pages contain local literal style tokens; no page-level Supabase theme override is applied.
3. **Settings coverage is narrow.** Only `index`, `about`, `contact`, and `proposal` directly load `site-settings.js`. Other pages do not receive these settings in the checked-in HTML. Its generic `page_content[path]` handles only one heading/subheading (`js/site-settings.js:84–90`), not arbitrary sections, metadata, forms, messages, imagery or footer. Extensionless paths and `.html` paths are not normalized to the same settings key. Truthy checks in `setText` and related overrides also prevent intentionally blanking existing copy.
4. **Navigation is split; footer is static.** Anonymous `.nav-links` can read `branding_content.nav` on loader-enabled pages. Signed-in menu labels/URLs, optional Host Center and Logout are hardcoded (`js/site-settings.js:34–62`). `.top`/other header structures are outside these selectors. `nav.html` and `footer.html` are build-time fragments, not Supabase consumers. Footer logos/copy/link groups/social/contact/copyright are repeated in many pages; only explicitly annotated email/phone nodes get contact overrides.
5. **Migration baseline is incomplete.** Many core tables are altered/read without a repository CREATE TABLE. Host/deals/trivia/operational tables are referenced in JS without migration evidence at all. `site_settings.home_content/about_content` and contact fields have ADD COLUMN evidence; `branding_content/page_content` do not. A clean-room schema cannot be verified from these migrations alone. Detailed per-query column evidence follows.
6. **Existing syntax blockers.** `public/host-center.html:5` has an unterminated single-quoted HTML string and duplicated/malformed trailing content around the closing document (`:9–12`). `api/submit/[type].js:192` uses an unescaped apostrophe in `traveler's` inside a single-quoted string. Strict JS parsing fails; tolerant extraction is only for inventory. This blocks trusting the affected workflow regardless of content storage.
7. **Potentially misleading auth/payment copy.** `public/account-confirmed.html:17–18,65–69` can claim confirmation on a direct no-token/no-session visit; its heading is always “Your email is confirmed.” even on error. `public/payment-result.html:9–10` defaults to “Payment submitted” with no record verification (only a cancellation query switch). Keep verification/authorization logic in code, but source approved pending/success/error wording from editable content and render it only for the verified state. No payment amounts or calculations are flagged here.
8. **Unwired wheel editor.** `public/admin.html:456–470` contains the Prize Wheel form but no root `js/` module reads/writes its controls or saves `wheel_settings`. `js/admin-promos.js` edits `discount_codes`, not wheel settings. Table Editor/Supamode may offer a path only if the live table, authorization, and Edge Function configuration match; that cannot be asserted from this tree.
9. **Stale campaign/time content.** Jamaica request deadline is November 2, 2026 (`public/jamaica-reopening-rush.html:7,26`), already past on the audit date. Atlanta options still include October 24 and November 7 (`public/atlanta-eat-sip-stay.html:56–57`); the Orlando payment page embeds dates (`public/pay/orlando-7q9k2m.html:45–46`). Legal “Last Updated” text and repeated © 2026 text are HTML literals. These dates have no content/data lifecycle binding. Do not infer availability from static marketing copy.

| public/about.html | 104 | Bound fallback: Our Story | site_settings.about_content.story_heading | HIGH |
| public/about.html | 106 | Bound fallback: At The Real Vacations, we believe that the best memories are made when we step away from the chaos of life and come together to experience something extraordinary. Whether it's a solo adventure, a couple's getaway, or a gathering of friends and family, we know that travel is about more than just a destination—it's about making meaningful connections, sharing laughter, and creating memories that last a lifetime. | site_settings.about_content.story[] | HIGH |
| public/about.html | 107 | Bound fallback: But here's the thing: we also know how stressful it can be to plan the perfect trip. Life is hectic. The constant juggling of work, schedules, and responsibilities leaves little room for much else. And when it comes to travel, finding the time, energy, and patience to plan a trip that everyone will enjoy can feel overwhelming. From booking flights to selecting the right hotel, arranging transportation, discovering great places to eat, and managing logistics, it can become more of a chore than a vacation. | site_settings.about_content.story[] | HIGH |
| public/about.html | 109 | Bound fallback: "Cates 26" | site_settings.about_content.story[] | HIGH |
| public/about.html | 109 | Bound fallback: For us, the desire to make travel easier was born from a simple family tradition that has been with us for over 20 years. Every December 26th, regardless of the circumstances, we gather as a family to create new memories, explore new places, and escape the stresses of daily life. We call it | site_settings.about_content.story[] | HIGH |
| public/about.html | 111 | Bound fallback: It serves as a reminder that, no matter how busy life gets, we must make time for the things that matter most. But as our family grew, so did the challenges of coordinating the perfect trip. We were a growing family—siblings, cousins, children—and booking for everyone felt like a never-ending puzzle. Flights, accommodations, transportation, finding the best places to eat, and all the details that come with planning a trip—it started to feel overwhelming. The joy of being together was quickly overshadowed by the stress of trying to make it all come together. | site_settings.about_content.story[] | HIGH |
| public/about.html | 112 | Bound fallback: And that's when The Real Vacations was born. | site_settings.about_content.story[] | HIGH |
| public/about.html | 113 | Bound fallback: I realized there had to be a better way—an easier, stress-free way to plan group trips without the endless back-and-forth between websites, the comparing of prices, or the anxiety of hoping everything would go smoothly. The Real Vacations was created to take that weight off your shoulders. | site_settings.about_content.story[] | HIGH |
| public/about.html | 114 | Bound fallback: We specialize in curated, all-inclusive group trips that make travel simple, affordable, and, most importantly, stress-free. Whether it's a family reunion, a company retreat, a group of friends, or even a destination music event like SweatFest Punta Cana, we handle all the details so you don't have to. Imagine a trip where you can simply show up, and the details—accommodations, transportation, event experiences, and optional flight-booking support—is already taken care of. No stress. No hassle. Just the freedom to enjoy the moment and each other's company. | site_settings.about_content.story[] | HIGH |
| public/about.html | 115 | Bound fallback: What's even better is that we offer customized group trips, designed specifically for your needs. Whether you're planning a family vacation where everyone can finally escape the everyday and enjoy quality time together, a team-building retreat for your company, or a celebration with friends, we curate experiences tailored to your unique group. From exclusive concerts and festivals to sporting events and cultural celebrations, we ensure your trip aligns with what you love most. | site_settings.about_content.story[] | HIGH |
| public/about.html | 117 | Bound fallback: Here's the relief: You won't have to spend hours, days, or weeks planning. No more endless searches or comparing prices. You won't have to worry about the details that usually leave you stressed and frustrated. | site_settings.about_content.story[] | HIGH |
| public/about.html | 117 | Bound fallback: We take care of everything, so you can focus on what really matters—the experience. | site_settings.about_content.story[] | HIGH |
| public/about.html | 119 | Bound fallback: We understand that the most valuable part of travel is the time you spend together. That's why we're here to ensure that you don't just get away, but you enjoy the journey—without all the anxiety. We offer flexibility in payments, allowing larger groups to plan without the burden of paying everything up front. Whether it's a family vacation, a corporate retreat, or a group of friends looking to reconnect, we make travel easy, affordable, and stress-free. | site_settings.about_content.story[] | HIGH |
| public/about.html | 120 | Bound fallback: The Real Vacations is about more than just a trip. It's about offering you comfort, relief, and that confidence that comes with knowing everything is taken care of. It's about giving you the freedom to create the memories you've been waiting for—without the stress, the frustration, or the confusion. | site_settings.about_content.story[] | HIGH |
| public/about.html | 121 | Bound fallback: So, are you ready to let go of the planning stress and finally have a vacation that's everything you've dreamed of? With The Real Vacations, your perfect trip is just a click away. We'll take care of the details, so you can focus on what truly matters—being together. | site_settings.about_content.story[] | HIGH |

| public/how-it-works.html | 102 | How It Works | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 103 | Group travel without the group headache. Here's the process. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 108 | The Booking Process | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 110 | Browse current TRV group experiences, or submit a travel request when you need a custom trip, flight, hotel, car, cruise, activity, or group plan built for you. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 110 | Choose a Trip or Request Your Own | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 111 | Create or sign in to your TRV account so your request, traveler details, quotes, approvals, payments, and trip status stay together in one secure place. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 111 | Use Your TRV Account | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 112 | Review Your Proposal | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 112 | When your quote is ready, TRV sends it to you for review. Open the full proposal, compare the available options and details, and submit your choice or approval from your account. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 113 | After approval, your booking and amount due appear in your TRV account. Depending on the trip or quote, you can pay in full or use the deposit and payment options shown at checkout. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 113 | Approve & Pay Securely | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 114 | TRV Handles the Details | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 114 | We coordinate the confirmed travel components, supplier details, payment status, and trip information tied to your booking. Your account remains your home base for updates. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 115 | Keep your trip details and payment status in your TRV account, watch for your confirmations and updates, and focus on enjoying the experience. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 115 | Travel & Enjoy | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 121 | Flexible Payment Options | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 123 | Deposit Booking | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 123 | When a trip or quote offers a deposit option, the required amount is shown before you complete checkout. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 124 | Break your trip cost into manageable monthly payments. Your automatic monthly payment schedule is shown before checkout, with the balance due no later than 60 days before departure. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 124 | Monthly Installments | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 125 | Pay in Full | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 125 | Prefer to handle everything at once? Pay in full at booking and you're all set. No more payments to worry about—just pack and go. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 131 | Frequently Asked Questions | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 133 | Inclusions vary by trip and by quote. The trip page or proposal shows the specific accommodations, transportation, tickets, activities, meals, or other services included in the option you are reviewing. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 133 | What's included in the trip price? | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 134 | Check the specific trip or proposal. Flights may be included, offered separately, or added to a custom request depending on the experience you are booking. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 134 | Do I need to book flights? | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 135 | What's your cancellation policy? | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 136 | Can I transfer my spot to someone else? | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 137 | Do you offer travel insurance? | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 137 | We partner with travel insurance providers and highly recommend purchasing coverage. Insurance protects you against unexpected cancellations, medical emergencies, and travel disruptions. We'll provide options at booking. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 138 | Solo travelers are welcome! Our prices are based on double occupancy, but we can arrange single room options (subject to availability and additional cost). Many solo travelers join our groups and make lifelong friends. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 138 | What if I'm traveling solo? | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 139 | Can TRV plan travel for my group? | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/how-it-works.html | 139 | Yes. Use Request Travel for a custom group trip and tell us what your group needs. TRV can build the proposal around the travelers, dates, services, and experience you request. | site_content[key=page.how_it_works].value.sections | HIGH |

| public/privacy-policy.html | 66 | Introduction | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/privacy-policy.html | 67 | The Real Vacations ("we," "our," or "us") operates the website therealvacations.com. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard your personal information when you visit our website, use our services, or book a trip with us. By using our website, you agree to the practices described in this policy. | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/privacy-policy.html | 69 | Information We Collect | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/privacy-policy.html | 70 | Information you provide directly: | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/privacy-policy.html | 70 | When you create an account, submit a travel request or contact message, approve a quote, book a trip, join a travel group, sign up for marketing, use Spin & Save, join VIP, or use a Host or supplier portal, we may collect information such as your name, email address, phone number, traveler details, trip preferences, communications, booking/payment status, and other information needed to provide the requested service. | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/privacy-policy.html | 71 | Information collected automatically: | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/privacy-policy.html | 71 | When you visit our website, we may automatically collect certain information including your IP address, browser type, device type, pages visited, time spent on pages, and referring URL. This information is collected through cookies and similar tracking technologies. | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/privacy-policy.html | 72 | Payment information: | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/privacy-policy.html | 72 | Payment transactions are processed through Stripe. The Real Vacations does not store your full credit card number, expiration date, or CVV on its own servers. Where you authorize future or installment payments, Stripe securely stores and processes the payment method and returns only limited payment-method information and identifiers to TRV. | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/privacy-policy.html | 74 | How We Use Your Information | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/privacy-policy.html | 75 | We use the information we collect to process and manage your trip bookings, communicate with you about your reservations and travel details, send you promotional offers, trip announcements, and newsletters (if you opted in), respond to your inquiries and provide customer support, improve our website and services, comply with legal obligations, and protect against fraud. | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/privacy-policy.html | 77 | Third-Party Services | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/privacy-policy.html | 78 | We work with trusted third-party services to operate our business. These services may have access to your personal information only to perform specific tasks on our behalf and are obligated to protect your data. | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/privacy-policy.html | 79 | Our current technology and service providers include: | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |

| public/privacy-policy.html | 84 | Email Communications | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/privacy-policy.html | 85 | If you explicitly opt in through our newsletter, account signup, Spin & Save, or another TRV marketing form, we may send marketing emails about upcoming trips, promotions, and travel updates. Transactional messages related to your account, quote, booking, payment, or trip may still be sent when necessary to provide the service you requested. | site_content[key=page.privacy].value.sections | HIGH |

| public/terms-of-service.html | 72 | The Real Vacations provides curated, all-inclusive group travel packages including accommodations, event tickets, transportation, and experiences. | public/terms-of-service.html | 76 | A booking is confirmed only after the applicable payment requirement is completed and TRV provides written booking confirmation. | public/terms-of-service.html | 78 | Travel Requests and Supplier Confirmation | site_content[key=page.terms].value.sections | HIGH |
| public/terms-of-service.html | 79 | When you submit a custom, concierge, or last-minute travel request, The Real Vacations begins work on your requested itinerary and supplier availability. | public/terms-of-service.html | 80 | Your request may be described as secured with TRV or awaiting supplier confirmation. | public/terms-of-service.html | 81 | Last-minute or expedited requests may include an additional professional service fee. Any applicable fee will be disclosed before payment is processed. ## Editability Gaps by Page
Every scored page is evaluated against all twelve requested checks below. “Partial” means source-wired only and inherits the deployment/schema caveats above. Metadata includes title and description; absence of a description is also a gap, not an editable empty state. No CSS theme is Supabase-bound. Generated text and record content can be editable even while the containing page fails.

## Admin UX Verification
These are source-backed capability assessments, not checkmarks from a live dashboard session. ✅ means a source path exists, contingent on schema/RLS/module deployment. An unchecked answer means the universal requirement is not implemented.

- [ ] Can an admin edit ANY visible text on ANY page without a developer?
  - NO. Only selected home/about/contact/heading and record fields are bound. All other headings/body/form/message/footer/meta values below need readers/editor support; missing public modules and incomplete schema compound this.
- [ ] Can an admin change a color/font/spacing without touching CSS?
  - NO for general site theme. No global_theme/page theme reader. wheel_settings prize segment colors are a narrow exception, not a global theme system.
- [ ] Can an admin add/remove a nav item without a deploy?
  - PARTIAL, not universally. branding_content.nav is saved by js/admin-content.js:436–449 and applied anonymously only by js/site-settings.js:67–78. Most checked-in pages lack that loader; authenticated menu is hardcoded; alternate .top headers are not targeted. Editor also requires at least one item and a nonempty logo/site name.
- [ ] Can an admin update a campaign banner without a deploy?
  - NO. Atlanta/Jamaica banners and injected JoinMyTrip host urgency campaign at js/site-settings.js:4–10 are literal; no campaign data reader/deadline visibility lifecycle.
- [ ] Can an admin change a form field label without a deploy?
  - NO generally. HTML labels/options/placeholder/consent and JS-generated form dictionaries are not content-bound. Saved form submissions do not make forms editable.
- [x] Can an admin update a trip/package price without a deploy?
  - SOURCE-SUPPORTED. Admin parses/saves trip_packages in js/admin-content.js:139–149,275–300; frontend uses table values. Table Editor can also edit authorized rows. Runtime unverified; keep validation/Stripe/financial logic in code.
- [x] Can an admin publish/unpublish a blog post without a deploy?
  - SOURCE-SUPPORTED. js/admin-content.js:356–387 saves is_published/published_at; content-public.js:161–164,323–325 filters publication state/date. Baseline columns and permissions require live verification.
- [ ] Can an admin change the spin wheel prizes without a deploy?
  - PARTIAL / UNVERIFIED. index/spin read wheel_settings, so an authorized Table Editor edit could update display if that live table exists. However public/admin.html:456–470 only supplies wheelForm markup; no wheelForm save listener or wheel_settings write exists in root js/. admin-promos.js edits discount_codes, not wheel settings. The table baseline, permissions, and deployed spin-wheel Edge Function prize issuance are unverified; no end-to-end working prize editor is demonstrated.
- [ ] Can an admin update legal page content without a deploy?
  - NO. privacy-policy.html and terms-of-service.html are static documents with no content loader or legal fields; a generic heading override cannot replace legal body/effective dates.
- [ ] Can an admin change error/success messages without a deploy?
  - NO. Local textContent/showState/Error/innerHTML and API-returned strings are literal. Supabase/Auth raw provider messages also have no editable localization/approved-message mapping.

Settings binding coverage: home JSON supports hero/trust/primary CTA/perks/steps/FAQs/selected headings/bottom copy; about supports hero/story/values/stats/CTA; contact supports heading/intro/email/phone/hours; branding supports selected nav logo/name/tagline/public nav/login/signup. None of these is a universal page/section/message/theme/metadata editor. JSON content changes do not by themselves create readers for new keys.

Storage bucket `.storage.from("content-media")` calls are not table references. Dynamic table calls are explicitly unresolved, not silently treated as existing.

None proves actual live existence. Nested selects are recursively checked by relationship/table name; FK disambiguation and live PostgREST schema cache/RLS are unverified. Insert/update payloads are not claimed fully validated by a SELECT-only check.

## Recommended Action Order

1. Restore/verifiably publish shared browser modules and resolve the two syntax blockers, then confirm existing read/write bindings work. Do not count existing settings as operational before this prerequisite.
2. Correct misleading confirmation defaults: distinguish verified/pending/expired/missing/no-session states. Keep state verification, auth, allowlists, prices, Stripe IDs/calculations and payment authorization in trusted code; only reviewed wording is editorial.
3. Capture the actual schema baseline and reconcile every absent/partial table and selected column below, then verify public-read/admin-write RLS. Confirm whether site_content exists live; if adopted, add a versioned migration/policies/seed contract instead of assuming it exists.
4. Define typed page content/message/theme contracts and readers (including metadata, image alt, form labels/options/consent, fallback text and legal documents). Prefer existing site_settings and record tables for existing bindings. Validate links and sanitize rich text; allow intentional empty copy without resurrecting immutable defaults.
5. Centralize public and signed-in navigation and full footer as runtime editable data across every header shape; avoid maintaining repeated embedded copies/build-time-only fragments as the content source of truth.
6. Move campaign headlines/cards/CTA/deadline/visibility, urgency announcements, trivia rules/dates and product affiliate destinations into content records; immediately review expired Jamaica and past Atlanta options. Do not move financial formulas or security rules into arbitrary CMS JSON.
7. Implement global_theme with a constrained token contract and justified per-page overrides, removing literal visual-token drift. Keep structural layout/security constraints in code.
8. Preserve working trip/package/resource/blog/gallery/testimonial/deal/wheel/VIP/host/supplier record flows while making all surrounding states, filters, category labels and empty-state copy editable; reconcile missing migration evidence rather than duplicating operational data into content JSON.
9. Verify with an authorized Table Editor/Supamode editor: change representative text, destination, image alt, form label, message, legal body, campaign deadline, nav item and theme token; reload every page without redeploying and verify anonymous/member/supplier/host states. Test missing/empty settings and RLS-denied paths. Document deploy-independent evidence and only then re-score.
